title: Cate's Base Camp: Wake up your English
description: «Cate's Base Camp» – the start of a new English learning path: You wake up the English you already know – school things, family words, numbers, colours and hobbies. You train am, is and are with the right pronouns, listen to a short dialogue and find out what you can already do. Level A1.

competencies.description: FS1E.1.A.1 (LiLe, Englisch 1. Fremdsprache – Hören): Die Schülerinnen und Schüler können verschiedenartige Hörtexte und Gespräche verstehen (Sachtexte, ästhetische Texte, Texte im Schulalltag, Gespräche im Kontakt mit Englisch sprechenden Personen).
FS1E.5.B.1 (LiLe, Englisch 1. Fremdsprache – Sprache(n) im Fokus, Wortschatz): Die Schülerinnen und Schüler verfügen über einen angemessenen Wortschatz, um sich mündlich und schriftlich zu äußern.

FS1E.5.D.1 (LiLe, Englisch 1. Fremdsprache – Sprache(n) im Fokus, Grammatik): Die Schülerinnen und Schüler können grammatische Strukturen in Texten erkennen und für das Verständnis nutzen sowie beim Sprechen und Schreiben anwenden.

FS1E.4.A.1 (LiLe, Englisch 1. Fremdsprache – Schreiben): Die Schülerinnen und Schüler können verschiedene Texte verfassen (Sachtexte, ästhetische Texte, Texte im Schulalltag, im schriftlichen Kontakt mit Englisch sprechenden Personen).

learningObjectives: I can introduce myself and say my name, my age and my hobby.
I can name school things, family words, numbers and colours in English.
I can use am, is and are with the right pronoun.
I can understand a short, simple dialogue when I listen.

blocks.title: Willkommen im Base Camp!
blocks.body:
Schön, dass du da bist! Ein Base Camp ist das Lager, in dem sich Bergsteigerinnen und Bergsteiger vor einer großen Tour sammeln – und genau das machen wir hier mit deinem Englisch. Du hast in der Primarschule schon viel Englisch gehört, gesungen und gesprochen. Das meiste davon ist noch da, versprochen – wir wecken es nur wieder auf.

In diesem Modul wirst du:

- **Wörter auffrischen**, die du schon kennst: Schulsachen, Familie, Zahlen, Farben und Hobbys,
- **am, is und are** mit den richtigen Pronomen üben,
- einen kurzen **Dialog anhören** und zeigen, was du verstehst,
- dich in ein paar Sätzen **selbst auf Englisch vorstellen**,
- am Ende beim **«Where do I stand?»-Check** herausfinden, was schon gut klappt.

Wichtig: Hier muss niemand perfekt sein. Ob du in der Primarschule viel oder wenig Englisch hattest – das Base Camp ist für alle der gleiche Startpunkt. Fehler sind erlaubt, Wiederholen ist erlaubt. Los geht's – have fun!

blocks.title: Grammar check: am, is, are
blocks.body:
**to be** means **sein** in German – and it is the most important verb in English. You only need three forms: **am**, **is** and **are**. The right form depends on the **pronoun** – the word for the person or thing:

| pronoun | form | example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I (ich) | **am** | I **am** happy. |
| you (du) | **are** | You **are** my friend. |
| he / she / it (er / sie / es) | **is** | She **is** my sister. |
| we (wir) | **are** | We **are** in the classroom. |
| you (ihr) | **are** | You **are** funny. |
| they (sie, Mehrzahl) | **are** | They **are** at home. |

**In short:** am goes with *I* – is goes with *he*, *she* and *it* – are goes with *you*, *we* and *they*.

When people speak, they often use short forms: *I'm* = I am, *she's* = she is, *we're* = we are. In the exercises here we write the long forms. The picture below shows you the rule.

blocks.title: am, is or are?
blocks.alt: Chart with three panels titled «to be». Blue panel «AM»: the pronoun I, with the example sentence «I am happy.» Green panel «IS»: the pronouns he, she, it, with the example sentence «She is my sister.» Orange panel «ARE»: the pronouns you, we, they, with the example sentence «We are friends.» Dark footer bar: «to be = sein · I am · he/she/it is · you/we/they are».
blocks.caption: Three forms, one rule: am goes with I, is goes with he, she and it, are goes with you, we and they.

blocks.title: Listening: Emma and Leo
blocks.vorleseText: Emma: Hi! I'm Emma. What's your name? Leo: Hello! My name is Leo. Nice to meet you! Emma: Nice to meet you too. How old are you, Leo? Leo: I am twelve. And you? Emma: I am eleven. Do you have brothers or sisters? Leo: Yes, I have two sisters. They are little – four and six. And you? Emma: I have one big brother. He is fourteen. Leo: What is your hobby? Emma: My hobby is swimming. I go to the pool every Friday. And your hobby? Leo: I like football and drawing. Emma: Cool! Oh, there is my bus. See you, Leo! Leo: Bye, Emma! See you!
blocks.description: Press play and listen carefully. Emma and Leo meet and talk. You can listen more than once. Then answer the questions below.

blocks.title: What did you hear?
blocks.intro: Four questions about Emma and Leo. You can go back and listen again before you answer.

questions.explanation: Leo says: «I am twelve.» Emma is eleven, and Emma's big brother is fourteen.
Emma says: «My hobby is swimming. I go to the pool every Friday.» Football and drawing are Leo's hobbies.

questions.prompt: How many sisters does Leo have?
questions.explanation: Leo says: «I have two sisters.» They are four and six years old.
At the end Emma says: «Oh, there is my bus.» The two children are talking at the bus stop.

blocks.title: Now you: introduce yourself
blocks.intro: Now it is your turn – like Alina, Emma and Leo.

tasks.prompt:
Write **three or four sentences about yourself**: your name, your age, your family or your hobby. Use **am, is** and **are**.

When you are done, check your text with this list:

- [ ] I wrote my name and my age.
- [ ] I wrote one sentence about my family or my hobby.
- [ ] I used am, is or are in every sentence.
- [ ] Every sentence starts with a capital letter.
tasks.hint: You can start like this: «Hi! I am …» – «I am … years old.» – «My hobby is …» – «This is my …»
tasks.solution: There is no single right answer – your text is about you! An example: «Hi! I am Lena. I am twelve years old. This is my family: my mum, my dad and my brother. My hobby is football.» Now compare: this example says the name and the age, one sentence is about the family, one is about a hobby, and every sentence uses am or is.

blocks.title: Where do I stand?
blocks.intro: This check is only for you. It is not a test. It shows you: What do I know? What can I practise again? Nobody sees your result – only you. Eight questions from the whole module – take your time!

questions.explanation: A ruler is a «Lineal». A pen writes, a chair is for sitting, and a book is for reading.
Your mother's mother is your grandmother – your grandfather is your mother's father. Your aunt and uncle are the sister and brother of your mum or dad.
Five plus seven is twelve – the same number as 5 + 7 = 12.
Black and white are opposites – like a chessboard.

questions.prompt: Choose the right form: «My brother … ten years old.»
questions.explanation: My brother = he, and he goes with is: «My brother is ten years old.» Am only goes with I, and are goes with you, we and they.
They goes with are: «They are my friends.» Is goes with he, she and it, and am only goes with I.

questions.prompt: Somebody asks you: «What's your name?» What do you say?
questions.explanation: «What's your name?» asks for your name, so you answer with it: «My name is Sam.» – «I am eleven» answers «How old are you?»
Swimming is a hobby – it is Emma's hobby in the dialogue. Your grandmother is a family word, a chair is a school thing, and white is a colour.

blocks.title: Extra challenge: have got
blocks.body:
Finished already? Then this extra part is for you – you do not need it to finish the module.

**have got** means **haben**. Maybe you remember the forms:

- I / you / we / they **have got** … → *I **have got** a blue school bag.*
- he / she / it **has got** … → *My aunt **has got** two cats.*

To make a **question**, you simply move *have* or *has* to the front:

- **Have** you **got** a pet? – Yes, I **have**. / No, I **haven't**.
- **Has** your brother **got** a bike? – Yes, he **has**. / No, he **hasn't**.

Maybe you noticed: In the dialogue, Emma asks «Do you have brothers or sisters?» – that is also correct English. Here you practise the second way: the question with **have got**.

Now it's your turn: a small writing task is waiting below.

blocks.title: Challenge: Three questions with have got
blocks.intro: A little writing challenge for fast climbers – optional, but fun!

tasks.prompt:
Write **three questions with have got** – about family, pets or school things. Then write a **short answer** for each question (Yes, … / No, …).

When you are done, check your text with this list:

- [ ] I wrote three questions with have got or has got.
- [ ] Every question starts with Have or Has and ends with a question mark.
- [ ] Every question has a short answer (Yes, … / No, …).
- [ ] Every sentence starts with a capital letter.
tasks.hint: You can start like this: «Have you got …?» – «Has your sister got …?» – «Has your teacher got …?» Useful words: a pet, a bike, a red pen, a big family, a little brother.
tasks.solution: There is no single right answer – your own questions are the goal. An example: «Have you got a pet? – No, I haven't. Has your brother got a bike? – Yes, he has. Has your teacher got a red pen? – Yes, she has.» Now compare: this example has three questions with have got or has got, every question starts with Have or Has and ends with a question mark, and every question has a short answer.
